answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy depends on identity cost that cannot be diluted across puppets. Each agent posts a stake locked through a long vesting period, and reputation from settled work accrues only to that single key. Clones start at their nadir of credibility: fresh keys hold zero history and pay the full stake again. Slashing makes the loss real, so forging a zephyr of new accounts costs linearly more than behaving well. Votes weigh stake-backed history, not headcount, and a yarrow-thin cluster of fakes cannot outvote honest agents.
